Line 61 is the assertion the row went looking for. Running that file with --reporter=verbose prints, by name, «sc-animal-hazard — trace gate > SHADOW replays with ZERO violations (doc 76 §5)» passing. The same run prints the identical row for sc-lane-control-signal, the row's other named exception. Both «exceptions» are gated by the same loop, so the row is 0 for 2. WHY THE STATIC AUDIT MISSED IT — THE JOIN KEY, NOT THE GATE, IS WHAT IS ABSENT. grep -c "sc-animal-hazard" on that test file returns 0. The file never writes either id as a literal: it imports REELS from ../scReels and iterates `for (const reel of REELS)`, naming each describe block through a template literal (${reel.id} — trace gate), so the ids exist only at runtime. scReels.ts:475 is where sc-animal-hazard enters that array (districtId ov-solid-v1, names [shadow-correct, mistake-swerve-oncoming, mistake-cross-line]) and scReels.ts:487 is sc-lane-control-signal. The file is untouched by repair rounds 1–6 (fad8af6 … 769bfd4, all 2026-08) and predates the wave-c filing by four weeks. Nothing was fixed here; the row was wrong when it was written. The proof is source text plus a deterministic recorder. I used no verdict, no score, no star count and no live drive, so the eight-run non-determinism problem does not reach this row: a recorded trace on a fixed district replays to the same bytes every time, which the byte-identity assertion independently demonstrates. It is not: the drive CRASHED INTO A BUILDING at t082s and the objective banner still says «Задача 2/3» on the final frame — the car never reached the mark, so the gate was never asked the question. An objective missed because the leg ended short of it is not the same fact as an objective that refuses a crawl, and only the second closes this row. THE MECHANISM IS UNREPAIRED AT THIS COMMIT, from the build's own source at ae87948b: templates-hazards2.ts:239-241 authors «Спри преди детето» as a BARE reachZone — {kind:"reachZone", x:4.06, y:146, radiusM:4, maxSpeedKmh:6} — with no requireVruUntouched, no requireNoContact and no dart witness of any kind; objectives.ts:1175 states in the build's own words that this title «does NOT match (no wait imperative)» the VRU demand; and objectives.ts:2488 computes done = reached && capMet && vruOk && contactOk && railOk && yieldOk, where the last four collapse to true for a zone that declares none of them. WORSE, THE WHOLE LESSON IS STILL CRAWLABLE: objective 3 «Изчакай детето…» DOES carry the derived demand, but vruWaitHonoured (objectives.ts:1531-1541) returns TRUE when stagedOutcomes holds no pedestrianDartOut — exactly the state a sub-25 км/ч crawl leaves it in. why: The stated mechanism is false: the award does not split by platform, it splits by FIRST PASS. platform/src/modules/gamification/xp.ts pays a sim lesson XP_SIM_COMPLETED 40 + (passed ? XP_SIM_PASSED_BONUS 60 : 0) + (passed && firstPass ? XP_SIM_FIRST_PASS_BONUS 50 : 0) + 10 per clean-drive commendation — and xpForEvent takes no platform argument of any kind, on any branch. 40+60 = 100; 40+60+50 = 150. The 50-XP gap the row read as a platform split is the one-time first-pass milestone, and the two re-drives show it doing exactly that: the PC leg pays 100 and its own debrief says it MATCHED an existing 0-point best (so not a first pass), while a mobile leg that had never passed before pays 150 and its debrief says the previous best was 9 points. In sweep161 the mobile leg was measured first, took the milestone, and the PC leg that followed could not. No stylesheet, no platform branch, no defect — an accounting artefact of measuring the same account twice.
